caption: The parity of a simple road is determined by the colors of its endpoints.
content: This page considers the number of cells a simple road passes through. For example, the road below passes through 11 cells in the Area.

In fact, if you only need to determine @b{whether the number of cells a road passes through is even or odd}, you don't have to count the road tiles. You can tell just by looking at @g{tips/complete_block/common/parity}{the colors of the cells}.
Since the color changes each time you move to an adjacent cell, @b{a simple road alternates between white cells @m{true} and black cells @m{false}}.
From this, we can derive the following properties about whether the number of cells a road passes through is even or odd.

items: If the endpoints of the road are @b{the same color}, the road passes through @b{an odd number of cells}.
If the endpoints of the road are @b{different colors}, the road passes through @b{an even number of cells}.

content: In the following examples, we use these properties by considering @g{tips/complete_block/common/parity}{whether the number of cells in the Area is even or odd}.

content.caption: Example 1
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.

To fill the Area with your available tiles, the only option is to create a simple road connecting @m{info}.
Since @b{the cells @m{info} are the same color}, the road must pass through @b{an odd number of cells}, no matter how it is laid out.

However, this Area has 24 cells (an even number), so a road that passes through an odd number of cells cannot fill the entire Area. No matter how the road is laid out, an odd number of cells will always remain.
Therefore, this Area cannot be completed.

content.caption: Example 2
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.

To fill the Area with your available tiles, the only option is to create a simple road connecting @m{info}.
Since @b{the cells @m{info} are different colors}, the road must pass through @b{an even number of cells}, no matter how it is laid out.

However, this Area has 23 cells to fill (excluding the one cell with a pre-placed tile), so a road that passes through an even number of cells cannot fill the entire Area. No matter how the road is laid out, an odd number of cells will always remain.
Therefore, this Area cannot be completed.
